Hi Laura,

Quick note — over the past 10 days our token usage on the production route has jumped ~2.7x compared to Jan averages. Latency has stayed acceptable, but we’re seeing queueing at peak and a couple of 5xx spikes. Our SREs suspect we’re hitting concurrency limits on the Dedicated pool.

Can Redwood provision additional GPUs for the next 30 days while we finish a model optimization project? Ideally +4 A100 equivalent for predictable throughput. We’re comfortable with a short-term commitment if it’s straightforward.

Attached is an anonymized export of last week’s request distribution (nimble_usage_feb.csv). We’ll share more metrics if helpful.

Thanks,

Hi Sahil — thanks for the data, that helps. We can absolutely support a short-term addendum while you complete optimizations. I have a few quick questions to size this properly:

- Is the 2.7x spike sustained across the workday or concentrated in two peak hours?
- Any change in typical sequence length (avg tokens/request)?
- Do you need exclusive GPUs (Dedicated tranche) or would burst capacity from shared pools be acceptable for 30 days?

Proposed near-term options (high level):
1) Temporary Dedicated tranche: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs, reserved for 30 days, with canary routing (start with 1 GPU for 24h).
2) Burst capacity: up to 4 GPUs on demand, slightly higher per-token cost but no reservation.

I can draft a formal addendum and pricing once we align. Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to review?

—Laura

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Observed usage spike — sizing & pricing input needed

Thanks for the ping, Laura. I pulled the attached usage summary and ran it against our throughput models. Short summary:

- The request distribution shows concentrated peak windows 11:30–13:00 and 15:30–17:00 PST. Average sequence length increased from ~220 tokens to ~310 tokens during peaks.
- For the service level they reported (95th p latency target ~250ms), +4 x A100-equivalent GPUs should cover steady-state peak concurrency if we route with continuous batching and enable their KV-prefix cache.
- Canary plan: start with 1 GPU for 24 hours (route 10% of traffic), then add 1 GPU/day until we hit 4, monitor p95 latency and queue depth.
- Risk: If sequence length remains >300 tokens and concurrency continues to climb, we may need an additional +1 GPU for headroom. Recommend a conditional clause in addendum for an extra GPU at pro-rated pricing.

Pricing guidance for 30-day reserved tranche (ballpark):
- +4 A100-eq (30 days): $19,200 (flat tranche fee) — includes 24/7 redwood monitoring and automated canary routing.
- Burst on-demand option (no reservation): estimated $0.55/token premium at current usage profile (customer to evaluate).

I attached a one-page sizing sketch. Happy to hop on the call and walk through the numbers.

—Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Capacity addendum proposal — NimbleDocs (RD-3421)

Hi Sahil / Elena — thanks for the call today. Per our conversation please find the proposed short-term addendum below:

Summary: 30-day reserved tranche of +4 A100-equivalent GPUs, 24-hour canary (10% traffic) then incremental roll to full tranche over 3 days. Conditional clause: if sustained average sequence length >300 tokens AND p95 latency exceeds 300ms for two consecutive business days, an optional +1 GPU can be added pro-rated at $4,800/month.

Pricing: +4 GPUs (30 days): $19,200 (one-time 30-day tranche fee). DocuSign link to sign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/placeholder-rd3421

Operational notes:
- Redwood will enable routing policy to send 10% of traffic to canary for 24h, then escalate to 25/50/100% over 3 days if metrics look good.
- We’ll enable KV-prefix caching and provide a short guide for client-side cache keys; Dev will help instrument metrics.
- Billing: one invoice for the addendum; credits applied for any unused days if the tranche is canceled early.

Attachments: proposed_addendum_v1.pdf (terms & pricing), sizing_sketch.pdf.

Next steps:
1) Please review the addendum and confirm by EOD Friday if you want DocuSign initiated.
2) If yes, sign and we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to enable canary routing and cache keys.

Happy to adjust language on the conditional clause if legal/procurement prefer different wording.

Best,
Laura Bennett
